statement.p: To estimate the health of the black-tailed deer population in the Jewell Meadow Wildlife Area, the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife caught, tagged, and released 84 black-tailed deer. A month later, they returned and observed 66 black-tailed deer, 6 of which had tags. Approximately how many black-tailed deer are in the Jewell Meadow Wildlife Area?

solution.p: Let x represent how many deer are in the Jewell Meadow Area. We set up a proportional equation: \begin{aligned} \frac{\text{tagged deer}}{\text{total deer}} \amp= \frac{\text{tagged deer}}{\text{total deer}}\\ \frac{6}{66} \amp= \frac{84}{x}\\ \frac{6}{66} \multiplyright{66\cdot x} \amp= \frac{84}{x}\multiplyright{66\cdot x}\\ 6 \cdot x \amp= 84\cdot 66\\ \divideunder{6 \cdot x}{6} \amp= \divideunder{84\cdot 66}{6}\\ x \amp= 924 \end{aligned} There are approximately 924 deer in the Jewell Meadow Area.
